Project Team and Roles Recipient Organization: City of Duluth For F3, the City of Duluth was the grant award recipient and co-Principle Investigator with Ecolibrium3, a community-based organization. Successful completion of the project involved cross-departmental coordination and community stakeholder and contractor management. Project members and roles included: Jim Benning, Director of Public Works and Utilities: Jim Benning provided project leadership and engineering technical expertise to the project, including participation in the Critical Infrastructure Team, representing the municipally- owned natural gas utility and public works. Benning stepped into the roles of co- principle investigator, business contact, and authorized representative upon the project departure of Mindy Granley. In these roles, he coordinated the completion of project deliverables, reporting, and grant close out. Mindy Granley, City of Duluth Sustainability Officer: Mindy Granley led the F3 project for the first six quarters as the co-principle investigator and authorized representative. She led the City of Duluth team focused on the asset-based planning approach, served as advisor to the community-based research. Her role included project design and grant compliance. Brett Crecelius, Community Resilience Project Coordinator: Brett Crecelius was hired by the City of Duluth to manage the asset-based approach and coordinate deliverable completion and grant reporting. Crecelius developed the site selection tool, city request for proposal for engineering and economic analysis, recruited partner communities, and wrote the Planning Toolkit. Upon completion of the Toolkit, Crecelius left the project for an economic development role in another state where he is incorporating project learnings. Ted Blenkush, Construction Project Coordinator: Ted Blenkush initially served on the city’s site selection team and was then brought onto the project in the final quarters of the grant award to complete the City portion of the scope of work. Blenkush oversaw final engineering and financial modeling for the selected city 25 sites, and has coordinated the City approach to solar development responses in alignment with the RACER results. Rob Morehouse, Deputy Fire Chief & Emergency Management Coordinator: Rob Morehouse provided project connection to existing emergency management approaches and plans. He served on the Critical Infrastructure Team and as City liaison to the community-based planning approach. Morehouse has served as an ongoing member of the Ready North Network and assisted in the development of the tabletop exercises that were used to advance integrated planning methodologies. Elena Foshay, Director of Workforce Development: Elena Foshay provided workforce data and assistance in evaluating workforce readiness for potential resilience solution sets. Sub-Recipient Organization- Ecolibrium3 Ecolibrium3 (Eco3) was the primary sub-recipient organization and a core partner to the City of Duluth for F3. Eco3's mission centers on leading change toward an equitable and sustainable future. Eco3 has expertise in weatherization, disaster recovery, climate resiliency, and solar projects and lead the development and execution of the community-based bottom-up methodology for resilience planning. Eco3 designed a community-based research plan, hired and trained canvassers to conduct on-the- ground research integrated into the community-based minimum resilience standards, and assisted in the development of the planning toolkit.
